t: Darius became king in 522 BCE by killing the ruler Gaumata, whom he called an impostor; his account of the events is generally regarded as a forgery that concealed the overthrow and murder of Cyrus's rightful successor Bardiya.
He put down revolts in most parts of the empire within a year, divided the empire into twenty satrapies with fixed tributes, and introduced the daric as a universal currency.

His campaigns took the empire to the Indus Valley and into Europe, but the expedition against Athens and Eretria ended in defeat at Marathon in 490 BCE, and he died in 486 BCE while preparing a second.
dyk: At Behistun, Darius had a trilingual inscription in Elamite, Old Persian and Babylonian carved into a cliff-face to record his conquests; it later became a key source for the Old Persian language and for the decipherment of cuneiform.
ev: Darius is born, the eldest son of Hystaspes
With six nobles he kills Gaumata at the fortress of Sikayauvati and takes the throne, then faces revolts in most parts of the empire
He campaigns in Central Asia, Aria and Bactria and winters in Gandhara before conquering the lands around the Indus River in 515 BCE
He crosses the Bosphorus on a bridge of boats and invades European Scythia, where the Scythians avoid battle
He travels to Egypt for the opening of the canal linking the Nile to the Red Sea
The Persian army sent against Athens and Eretria is defeated at the Battle of Marathon
Darius dies after a revolt in Egypt delays his planned expedition; Xerxes succeeds him

f.born: c. 550 BCE; the eldest of five sons of Hystaspes, an Achaemenid noble and officer in Cyrus's army, and grandson of Arsames; his mother is variously given as Rhodogune or Irdabama
f.died: 486 BCE, after thirty days of an unidentified illness, aged about sixty-four; his body was embalmed and entombed in October 486 BCE in the rock-cut tomb at Naqsh-e Rostam
f.role: Lance-bearer (spearman) to Cambyses II; King of Kings of the Achaemenid Empire from 522 BCE until his death in 486 BCE
f.known: the killing of Gaumata and the revolts of 522 BCE; the Behistun Inscription; the satrapies and the daric; the Indus Valley and Scythian campaigns; the Darius Canal; the punitive expedition against Eretria and Athens ending at Marathon; the rock-cut tomb at Naqsh-e Rostam
